([Meeting Recording](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11HoFAxbT_x49F-Qd2pchLgvA3nFRsmvM/view?usp=sharing) **⭕** / [Meeting Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NwBMQewZWXelo6MYKpHRwRocSXSapChK_9vnNlSOL0Q/edit?usp=sharing))

- Highlights

      - Apache Iceberg 1.3.0 has been released ð ð¥³
      - Added encryption key and AAD to Parquet write builders (Thanks, Gidon!)
      - Spark 3.4 supports timestamp_ntz (Thanks, Fokko!)
      - Rebuilt Spark MERGE file handling (Thanks, Anton!)
  - Releases

      - PyIceberg 0.4.0 release
  - Discussion

      - Adaptive split planning in core and Spark ([PR #7714](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/7714), [PR #7731](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/7731))
      - [Multi-table transactions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UxXifU8iqP_byaW4E2RuKZx1nobxmAvc5urVcWas1B8/edit#heading=h.6sa1rpsxiuke) Catalog API ([PR #7741](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/7741))
      - Incremental scan API ([PR #6182](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/6182))
      - Views status update
      - Partition stats ([PR #7105](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/7105))
      - Metadata deletion and gc.enabled
  - AI Summary

      - Daniel, Dmitri, and Jack discussed various updates and improvements to different tools and systems, including the release of Apache iceberg 1.3, progress on encryption, the addition of UID and timestamp support in Spark, and an overhaul of file handling in Spark's merge plan. They also mentioned the need to discuss these updates further in the train-out community. - PLAY @0:03:
      - Jack suggests sharing their data preparation process with the Spark community. - WATCH (30 secs):
      - The group discussed different approaches to split planning for parallelism in Spark, including adapting split sizes based on the amount of data and creating larger splits for larger scans. They also considered the right amount of parallelism and balancing the number of workers with the number of parents to achieve cost savings. - PLAY @5:55:
      - The group discussed various topics including adaptive split planning and multi-table transactions with extensions to the catalog API. They considered different approaches and methods for implementation, with Fokko expressing satisfaction with the new multi-table API. - PLAY @16:41:
      - Jack, Fokko, and others discussed various topics such as multi-table swaps, incremental change log scan with deletes, partition stats, and publishing stats. They explored the possibility of putting additional stats like NDVs in the manifest level, but faced challenges in tracking sketches and inflating metadata size. They considered options like partition level stats and table level NDVs, and suggested calculating NDVs for individual partitions to weigh off in the estimate. - PLAY @27:00:
      - Jack and Daniel discussed the importance of tracking statistics like NDV and in-memory column size at the partition level. They also talked about the GC-enabled property and how it applies to tables that don't own their own files. - PLAY @37:35:
      - The group discussed the issue of metadata file deletion and whether it should be controlled by GC-enabled. They considered various options, including leaving all garbage files and having a flag to stop any cleanup, but ultimately decided that changing the behavior of the library for something that violates the spec would be problematic. PLAY @47:17:

They also mentioned plans for engine integrations and the need for further discussions on multi-table transactions.

      - Proposal for process to improve communication and documentation of changes in Iceberg [bits]

          - Why? Let’s make a better developer and contributor experience!

              - Missing [documentation for features](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/commit/d8a07ff276dc0efbfbbe3df3579c638c863b2686)

          - Discuss a central location to track proposals [JB, bits]

              - GitHub Issues w/“proposal” label?
          - Some ideas gleaned from the Trino project

              - Keep a running list of merged PRs[ in the description of the pull request that updated the release notes](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/pull/19497) and add these PRs to the release milestone (ex. [1.4.0](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/milestone/35?closed=1))
              - Add a PR template with a release notes and docs section. Also add checkboxes to communicate that the commit(s) are not a user-facing change, and no release notes/docs are needed
